data.title: bn-3a9sr: CML run configuration schema, strict reader and configured lowering (RFC 0003 corr. 3)

data.body:
[MEDIUM][CWE-400] Schema-valid configurations can bypass the intended linear work bound here. After typecheck proves membership, each element constant searches the full element vector with position. Many constants bound to a late element therefore cost constants times elements. The fuel charge happens only after each scan. It counts index positions, not compared name bytes. MAX_SORT_ELEMENTS allows 65,536 entries, while the document permits many constants. The current linearity test uses one Set[Nat] constant and never enters this path.

Failure modes: configured lowering can monopolize CPU or report WorkLimitExceeded only after doing the work.
Edge cases: late elements, long names, many same-sort constants, and nearly exhausted fuel maximize the gap.
Rollback: revert configured lowering or keep it unavailable until indexing is bounded.
Monitoring: track lowering latency, config counts, and work-limit refusals. Usage currently undercounts this scan.
Validation: build a name-to-index map once, precharge its build and lookups, then add two-axis scaling and tight-fuel tests.
Counterevidence: current repository call sites are tests only. This limits exposure evidence, but the public API accepts untrusted artifact data by design.

[LOW][CWE-770] The returned identities allocate two full configuration-sized byte vectors without metering them. RunIdentity::of copies the configuration identity, then Configured clones ConfigIdentity. The only burn covers model identity bytes. ConfigValue::size at config.rs:103-121 also counts a Str of any length as one node. An unused near-16 MiB string constant can therefore fit a tiny semantic charge and still add about two configuration-sized output allocations. MAX_CONFIG_BYTES bounds one request, but Limits and Usage do not bound or report these copies.

Failure modes: memory amplification and misleading budget evidence.
Edge cases: unused large strings and repeated concurrent lowerings maximize allocations.
Rollback: disable configured lowering or omit owned returned identities until charges exist.
Monitoring: compare input bytes, identity bytes, RSS, node usage, and concurrent calls.
Validation: charge string and key text plus both identity copies before allocation. Add a low-node-limit long-string regression.
Counterevidence: the 16 MiB parser limit caps per-call amplification. This makes the finding low severity, not unbounded OOM.

data.reason: BLOCK: unresolved [MEDIUM] postcharged superlinear element indexing and [LOW] unmetered identity-copy amplification. Static Seal review does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: Fixed in 24c3f97. Each sort (and enumeration) gets one name-to-index table, built only after its charge (a sort over the names' bytes). Element and variant lookups are logarithmic and charged by name length before they are made; the position scan is gone. The missing/extra checks and sort-typed nodes now charge lookups by the actual name length. Tests: element_constants_cost_a_table_lookup_not_a_scan (two axes, operation-counted; restoring position makes per-constant work grow 1.99x per sort doubling and the test fail), a_tight_work_limit_is_refused_before_any_element_lookup, the_configured_boundary_is_exact.

Fixed in 24c3f97. ConfigValue::size charges strings, element and variant names, and record field names by bytes; stored bindings charge their names. RunConfig holds its identity in an Arc: Configured and RunIdentity share it and never copy its bytes; RunIdentity holds the model identity by value (its bytes charged as output and work, so they appear in Usage) and encodes on request. Tests: long_string_constants_are_charged_by_their_bytes (1 MiB string refused under a 10 000-node limit), the_configured_boundary_is_exact (one node or one work unit below measured usage is refused).

[RESOLVED] The target now precharges table construction at crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:559-583 and every element lookup at lower.rs:680-686. The position scan is absent. The two-axis and tight-fuel tests cover the prior path.

data.reason: Verified at 24c3f97: precharged name-to-index tables replace the postcharged linear scan.

data.body:
[LOW][CWE-770] The Arc change removes both configuration-identity copies, and ConfigValue::size now counts owned text. However, the model identity allocation is still postcharged. lower.rs:480 calls Model::identity before lower.rs:482-487 checks either the node or work budget. Model::identity allocates the full encoding and per-action outcome buffers. A limit that is one unit short therefore refuses only after the memory and work occur. The exact-boundary test confirms the result, but it does not prove preallocation refusal.

Failure modes: a large lowered model can exceed the requested memory or work envelope before returning OutputTooLarge or WorkLimitExceeded.
Edge cases: many initial states, many actions, large expressions, and concurrent calls maximize the unreported peak.
Rollback: keep configured lowering unavailable, or return the model without constructing its identity until a precharge exists.
Monitoring: compare model cardinalities, identity bytes, peak RSS, latency, and refusal usage.
Validation: measure the identity size without allocation, reserve node and work budgets first, then encode. Add a near-maximum model test whose insufficient limit proves the encoder was not entered.
Counterevidence: repository call sites remain tests, and existing model bounds cap one call. Those facts limit exposure but do not make Limits enforce the documented precharge contract.

[LOW][CWE-400] ConfigValue::size creates an explicit Vec at config.rs:111 and extends it across every child at config.rs:121-133. lower.rs:630 calls this full traversal before charge or burn. A wide schema-valid value can therefore consume linear CPU and width-proportional scratch memory even when nodes or work is zero. Usage reports none of that work.

Failure modes: a caller can bypass a configured lowering limit and cause CPU and scratch-memory amplification before a typed refusal.
Edge cases: wide sets, sequences, maps, many constants, tiny Limits, repeated calls, and concurrent calls maximize the gap.
Rollback: keep configured lowering unavailable, or remove the unmetered sizing prepass.
Monitoring: compare configuration bytes and value counts with Usage, latency, allocation peaks, and refusal rates.
Validation: compute and store the measure during bounded parsing, or meter an allocation-free traversal before each proportional allocation. Add a wide-value test with zero or tiny limits that proves refusal precedes traversal and scratch growth.
Counterevidence: MAX_CONFIG_BYTES caps one configuration at 16 MiB, and current repository call sites are tests. This bounds one call but does not make Limits effective.

data.reason: BLOCK: unresolved [LOW][CWE-770] postcharged model-identity encoding at lower.rs:480-487 and [LOW][CWE-400] unmetered ConfigValue::size traversal at config.rs:108-137. The element-table finding is resolved. Static Seal review does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: Fixed in e118015. continuum-model-core gains Model::identity_len_bound, an allocation-free upper bound on the identity encoding (exact without duplicate outcomes; unit test the_length_bound_is_exact_or_above). lower_configured charges the bound's walk (at most the charged nodes plus initial-state values, variables, actions, predicates), then the bound as output and work, before Model::identity runs, and debug-asserts the encoding fits. Test the_model_identity_is_charged_before_it_is_built: one node or one work unit short is refused and the thread-local counter identity_encodings_on_this_thread shows identity() never ran; moving identity() before the charge makes it fail. model-core is listed in the GOV record.

Fixed in e118015. Each constant's size is computed once while the document is read (bounded by the reader's depth and 16 MiB caps) and stored; RunConfig::constant_size is a map lookup, charged in lowering by name length. ConfigValue::size is now private to the reader. The declared sort and constant indexes in bindings are also charged before they are built. Test: constant_sizes_are_stored_at_read_time.

[RESOLVED] e118015 computes each configuration value size during bounded parsing at crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/config.rs:244-251, stores it in RunConfig, and lower_configured uses the lookup at crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:661-668. No value-width traversal remains before the lowering charge.

data.reason: e118015 stores each value size during bounded parsing and lower_configured performs only a charged lookup.

data.body: [LOW][CWE-770][STILL OPEN] e118015 precharges one final identity length at crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:505-509, but Model::identity still allocates a Vec for every encoded outcome at crates/continuum-model-core/src/identity.rs:86-98 while the final output Vec is live, then copies those bytes into it at identity.rs:101-104. The comment at lower.rs:490 calls this one allocation, but it is not. Failure modes: Limits can admit the final identity while actual identity construction also holds an unmetered outcome buffer and its vector storage. Edge cases: one action with many assignments, long names, large expressions, and concurrent lowerings maximize the extra live memory. Rollback: keep configured lowering unavailable, stream deterministic outcomes directly, or charge temporary outcome encodings before identity construction. Monitoring: compare identity_len_bound, peak RSS, allocation bytes, action outcome sizes, and concurrent calls. Validation: instrument identity allocation bytes and prove a tight limit refuses before both final and temporary buffers, including one large deterministic outcome. Counterevidence: configured lowering produces one outcome per action and model limits cap one call, so amplification is bounded; the resource contract remains false.

[MEDIUM][CWE-20] The normative schema requires variant.name to match identifier at notes/plan/schemas/run-config.schema.json:163-168, but this shared elem-or-variant branch validates every name with is_name. RunConfig::parse therefore accepts values such as variant name bad-name or 1 and mints ConfigIdentity even though the schema rejects them. Failure modes: a schema-invalid artifact crosses the public reader boundary and can be stored, compared, or trusted as a valid run configuration before lowering later rejects it. Edge cases: leading digits and printable punctuation all pass is_name but fail the identifier pattern; valid element names must remain printable names. Rollback: do not expose this reader as schema-conforming until variant names use is_identifier, while element names keep is_name. Monitoring: differentially compare parser acceptance with Draft 2020-12 validation and count parity failures by JSON path. Validation: add parser cases for bad-name and 1 under variant.name, require cml.config.shape, and retain a valid Busy variant case through lower_configured. Counterevidence: current lowering rejects unmatched invalid names as ill-typed, but parse success and ConfigIdentity creation already violate the normative acceptance boundary.

data.reason: MEDIUM schema-reader divergence accepts schema-invalid enum variant names; LOW identity construction still allocates unmetered temporary outcome buffers.

data.body: Fixed in 124768f. Variant names are read as CML identifiers (element names stay printable-ASCII names). Audit of every field against the schema found one more divergence: under Python's re, $ accepts a trailing line feed, so the name and identifier patterns gain a (?!\n) guard (same meaning under ECMA-262). Differential: notes/plan/tools/run_config_parity.py generates 197 cases (both committed fixtures plus edge names and shapes for every constrained field; 82 accepted) with each document's Draft 2020-12 verdict under the schema's stated document profile (strict JSON lexicon, set/map duplicates by value); validate_dossier.py (just dossier) fails if the corpus is stale; configured.rs::the_reader_agrees_with_the_schema_on_every_parity_case requires RunConfig::parse to match every verdict. Reverting to is_name for variants fails it on 1a, a-b, bad-name, 1. The 16 MiB and depth-64 caps are resource bounds outside both, documented in schemas/README.md.

Fixed in 124768f, structurally in continuum-model-core: Model::identity writes each action's outcomes into one reused scratch buffer as byte ranges (sorted and deduplicated by their bytes), with no Vec per outcome, and allocates the output, scratch, and range buffers once at their bounds, so none grows. Model::identity_alloc_bound bounds the peak (output + largest action's outcomes + 16 bytes per outcome); lower_configured charges all five walks and that bound before the encoding, and the comment at lower.rs now states exactly that. continuum-model/1 bytes unchanged: tests/identity_golden.rs pins a model exercising every encoding branch (written by the old encoder), and the DieHard differential identity tests still pass.

[RESOLVED][MEDIUM][CWE-20] At target 124768f, crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/config.rs:513-558 keeps element names under is_name and validates variant names with is_identifier. notes/plan/schemas/run-config.schema.json:52-60 and :124-174 now match those rules, including the trailing-line-feed guard. notes/plan/tools/run_config_parity.py:164-266 covers every constrained name and shape, and crates/continuum-cml-elab/tests/configured.rs:469-513 binds its committed verdicts to RunConfig::parse.

data.reason: Verified at 124768f: the reader and normative schema now agree for variant names and the full committed parity corpus.

data.body: [RESOLVED][LOW][CWE-770] At target 124768f, crates/continuum-model-core/src/identity.rs:76-115 allocates only the final output, one reused outcome scratch buffer, and one range buffer. identity.rs:134-166 bounds all three. crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:487-515 charges five model walks and the allocation bound before identity() runs. Failure modes: schema drift, budget bypass, or identity-byte drift now fail the parity, precharge, or golden controls. Edge cases: invalid names, trailing line feeds, wide configurations, duplicate outcomes, long expressions, and maximum model cardinalities are covered by bounded readers or structural bounds. Rollback: revert the configured-lowering range or keep lower_configured unavailable if any control regresses. Monitoring: track parity disagreements, typed refusals, Usage, identity sizes, latency, and peak RSS. Validation: I inspected the whole persisted range and exact target; committed parity, golden, boundary, allocation-bound, and pre-encoding tests cover the changed paths. This static LGTM does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.reason: Verified at 124768f: one prebounded output, scratch, and range allocation replaces per-outcome buffers, and lower_configured precharges the full bound.
LGTM at 124768f after whole-range review. The schema-reader parity and identity-allocation findings are resolved. Static approval preserves the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.
